source_cards.front: What steps does a driver take when approaching a left turn?
source_cards.back: Approaching a left turn, signal three to five seconds in advance, slow gradually while checking the rearview mirror to confirm the driver behind understood, make sure no bicyclist or vehicle behind is trying to pass on your left, and on a multilane road be in the left lane well ahead of the turn without moving suddenly from the right lane.

source_cards.front: In what order does a driver search before a right turn, and to whom must the driver yield?

source_cards.front: What following distance does the four second method give, and when is more needed?
source_cards.back: The four second method leaves enough room to stop quickly behind the vehicle ahead, and when the road is poor, visibility is poor or speeds are higher the gap should grow beyond four seconds.

source_cards.front: How is the four second following distance measured against a checkpoint?
source_cards.back: To measure four second spacing, note when the rear of the vehicle ahead passes a checkpoint such as a sign, driveway, pole or parked vehicle, count seconds until your vehicle reaches it, and fewer than four seconds means you are following too closely and must drop back.

source_cards.front: What is an easy way to count seconds for following distance?

source_cards.front: How do reaction distance and braking distance differ, and how do wet, icy, or gravel roads affect braking distance?
source_cards.back: Reaction distance is traveled from seeing danger until stepping on the brake, whereas braking distance is traveled from applying the brakes until stopping and becomes much longer on wet, icy, or gravel roads.

source_cards.front: What is braking distance, and when does it grow much longer?
source_cards.back: Braking distance is the distance traveled from the moment the brakes are applied until the vehicle stops, and it becomes much longer on wet, icy or gravel roads.

source_cards.front: Why is the road especially slippery when rain first begins?
source_cards.back: When rain first begins, oil, rubber, dirt and water mix to make the road especially slippery, which increases braking distance.
